title: Python ctypes enables C/C++ interop for performance-critical loops
claim: ctypes module allows calling compiled C code from Python without subprocess overhead, enabling optimization of hot paths via direct FFI.
support: Detailed code examples showing C struct mapping and function binding.
mechanism: Direct shared library calls bypass Python interpreter for numeric-heavy operations.
assumptions: C code is compiled and available as shared object
failure_modes: Mismatch between C struct layout and Python ctypes definition
Platform-specific ABI differences
validation: Can be tested by benchmarking ctypes vs pure Python on integer sequence operations.

title: Project templates favor pytest, Flake8, and coverage.py for test automation
claim: Analysis of 18 Python project templates on GitHub found >50% adoption of pytest, Flake8, and coverage.py tooling, suggesting these are de facto standards for production Python projects.
support: Survey of GitHub templates; quantitative justification provided.
mechanism: Community consensus on tooling reduces friction for new contributors and maintains code quality.
assumptions: GitHub templates are representative of production practices
failure_modes: Templates may reflect fashion rather than actual project needs
validation: Can replicate template analysis with current GitHub data; may find shifts toward newer tools.

title: CNN-based object detection requires decomposition into preprocessing, detection, tracking, and inference steps
claim: Parking space detection pipeline decomposes into five steps: frame capture, parking space recognition, vehicle detection, occupancy classification, and alert generation.
support: Concrete worked example with pipeline architecture.
mechanism: Modular decomposition allows independent optimization of each component and enables reuse.
assumptions: Each step can be independently validated
failure_modes: Errors in early steps (e.g., parking space detection) cascade to downstream steps
validation: CNN pipelines for trading signal generation can adopt similar decomposition; each component's precision/recall can be measured independently.

title: ML pipeline accuracy depends on each component's precision in isolation
claim: CNN parking detection achieves high overall accuracy only if each stage (parking space detection, vehicle detection, occupancy classification) maintains acceptable precision independently; error propagation through stages reduces final accuracy.
support: Implicit in pipeline design; not explicitly quantified in text.
mechanism: Conditional probability: P(correct final prediction) = P(step1 correct) * P(step2 correct | step1 correct) * ...
assumptions: Errors in stages are conditionally independent (may not hold in practice)
failure_modes: Systematic bias in one stage causes failures across all predictions
validation: Backtest validation frameworks should decompose signal generation into steps and measure precision per step.

title: Options are contracts giving the right (not obligation) to buy or sell at a strike price before expiration
claim: A call option grants the right to purchase 100 shares at a fixed strike price on or before the expiration date. A put option grants the right to sell.
support: Textbook definition; repeated across financial references.
mechanism: Optionality creates asymmetric payoff: buyer gains from favorable moves, seller receives premium regardless of outcome.
failure_modes: Non-standard contracts (single-share, variance swaps) differ significantly
validation: Confirmed against OCC specifications and broker documentation.

title: Options provide leverage relative to stock ownership
claim: Buying call options provides similar directional exposure to stock with lower capital outlay; buyer profits 80% of a dollar move on the stock at much lower cost than equivalent shares.
support: Statement attributed to 'Allen Everhart' on deep-in-the-money call strategies.
mechanism: Option premium is lower than stock price; leverage effect from optionality; delta approximately equal to in-the-money call.
assumptions: Deep-in-the-money calls have high delta (~0.8+) and low theta decay
failure_modes: Out-of-money or near-the-money calls have low delta and high theta decay
Wide spreads on options reduce leverage advantage
validation: Hypothesis: deep ITM call alpha = stock alpha; testable via backtest comparing payoffs.

title: Options Greeks (delta, theta, gamma, vega) quantify exposure sensitivities
claim: Delta measures directional exposure; theta measures time decay; gamma measures delta sensitivity; vega measures volatility sensitivity.
support: Textbook definitions; standard option pricing framework.
mechanism: Black-Scholes and other pricing models decompose option value into directional and volatility components.
assumptions: Greeks are computed under Black-Scholes assumptions (log-normal distribution, no dividends, constant volatility)
failure_modes: Greeks assume continuous trading and risk-neutral valuation; real markets have gaps and jump risk
validation: Greeks can be computed and backtested; verify against market data and IV term structures.

title: Selling options (short) increases risk relative to buying options (long)
claim: The book distinguishes short (naked call) from long (call buying): short options require capital to cover potential assignment; long options limit losses to premium paid. This distinction suggests different risk profiles and margin requirements.

source.section: Misconception #3: Option selling is more profitable

support: Text describes margin requirements and assignment risk for short options.
mechanism: Short options have unlimited loss potential; long options have limited loss (premium paid).
assumptions: Standard equity options; assignment rules as defined by OCC
failure_modes: Portfolio margin or box spreads can change capital requirements dramatically
validation: Backtest framework must track margin requirements and assignment scenarios separately for long vs short.

title: Common options strategies include covered calls, spreads, and collars
claim: Covered call: own stock, sell call above current price. Spread: buy call at lower strike, sell call at higher strike. Collar: own stock, sell call, buy put.
support: Textbook definitions; widely used in practice.
mechanism: Each strategy manages different risk/reward profiles: covered call generates income, spread limits max gain, collar hedges downside.
assumptions: Strategies assume liquid options markets and standard contract terms
failure_modes: Illiquid underlyings make strategies expensive to execute; early assignment affects outcomes
validation: Backtest each strategy against historical data; measure Sharpe, max drawdown, and execution costs.

title: Successful traders manage risk, accept losses, and learn from failures
claim: Traders must understand risk tolerance, use discipline to limit losses, and treat failures as learning opportunities. Quotes from Martin Schwartz (1984 champion) and Brett Steenbarger emphasize continuous improvement and avoiding overtrading.

source.epub_locator: Trader psychology and risk management discussion

support: Anecdotal quotes from well-known traders; not empirically validated.
mechanism: Risk awareness and loss acceptance reduce catastrophic drawdowns; learning feedback loops improve strategy robustness.
assumptions: Anecdotes from successful traders are generalizable
failure_modes: Selection bias: book highlights winners, not failures
validation: Cannot be directly validated from book; relevant to operational design (e.g., maximum daily loss limits, position-size rules).

title: Option selection heuristics (deep ITM, high delta) prioritize intrinsic value over optionality
claim: The book recommends selecting deep-in-the-money calls with 70+ delta to simplify strategy and reduce theta decay exposure; this strategy treats options like leveraged stock with reduced theta risk.

source.section: How to Select the Right Option for Major Gain

support: Recommendation to buy 70-delta calls; claim that 'you don't need to worry much about theta decay.'
mechanism: High delta = stock-like behavior; ITM options have lower theta per unit delta.
assumptions: Liquidity and spreads are narrow for deep ITM options
failure_modes: ITM options are more expensive; delta approaches 1, reducing leverage advantage
validation: Backtest: compare payoff and Sharpe of deep ITM vs ATM vs OTM calls on same underlying.

title: Avoid random exercise of short options by using defined-risk strategies
claim: When holding 200 short option positions, random overnight assignment of a dozen positions creates surprise inventory. Use simple strategies (e.g., deep ITM calls) to avoid exercise risk.

source.section: Important Tips & Tricks about Options Trading

support: Anecdotal example of operational risk from unplanned assignment.
mechanism: Assignment of short options creates forced inventory changes; unexpected assignments disrupt day-to-day risk models.
assumptions: Short stock or portfolio positions are not hedged
failure_modes: Assignment is actually predictable via dividend dates, early exercise, and Greeks
validation: Test live system's handling of unexpected assignment; verify clearing house notifications and position reconciliation.

title: American options allow exercise at any time; European options only at expiration
claim: American option holders can exercise on any business day through expiration; European option holders can only exercise on expiration date.
mechanism: American optionality is more valuable; European optionality is simpler to model.
failure_modes: Exotic options (Bermuda, Asian) have intermediate exercise rules
validation: Confirmed against OCC specifications; verify broker documentation for exercise windows.

title: Day trading and swing trading operate on different timeframes
claim: Day trading: hold positions for hours to one day. Swing trading: hold days to weeks. Scalping: seconds to minutes. Position trading: weeks to years/months.

source.section: Difference between swing trading and day trading

support: Table with time frames for each style.
mechanism: Timeframe determines relevant risk factors: intraday volatility, overnight gaps, corporate events, macro regimes.
assumptions: Timeframes are fixed; no hybrid strategies
failure_modes: Strategies may have mixed timeframes (e.g., day trade exits, swing trade entries)
validation: Backtest signal generation and rebalancing logic; measure turnover, holding periods, and slippage by timeframe.

title: Trading strategy has three phases: planning, placing, executing
claim: A structured trading process involves: (1) plan trade (analysis, position sizing, risk tolerance), (2) place trade (order entry), (3) execute trade (monitor, adjust, exit).
mechanism: Disciplined process reduces emotional decisions and improves consistency.
failure_modes: Emergency exits or forced liquidations break the plan
validation: Backtest and live execution logs can be analyzed to verify adherence to planning phase.

title: Trading strategies often use support/resistance levels and breakout signals
claim: Common entry signals: price breaks above resistance or below support. Exit signals: price returns to support/resistance or technical indicators reverse.

source.section: Swing trading and day trading: tactics and strategies

support: Described strategies without quantitative definition or backtesting evidence.
mechanism: Support/resistance levels aggregate historical turning points; breakouts indicate momentum shift.
assumptions: Support/resistance are stable; market participants respect these levels
failure_modes: Levels are subjective and may not hold after market structure changes; false breakouts common
validation: Backtest: define support/resistance programmatically (e.g., local minima/maxima) and measure breakout Sharpe and win rate.

title: Common technical indicators include RSI, MACD, and Bollinger Bands
claim: RSI (Relative Strength Index): momentum indicator, overbought >70, oversold <30. MACD (Moving Average Convergence Divergence): trend indicator. Bollinger Bands: volatility indicator, price bands +/- 2 std devs from MA.
support: Standard technical analysis definitions; widely used.
mechanism: Each indicator summarizes price/volume history to identify overbought/oversold or trend conditions.
assumptions: Indicators are computed over standard periods (14-day RSI, 12/26-day MACD, 20-day BB); thresholds (>70 overbought) are universal
failure_modes: Parameters are arbitrary; no evidence these thresholds outperform alternatives
validation: Backtest different indicator parameters and thresholds; measure Sharpe, max drawdown vs random signals.

title: Day trading and swing trading have different risk/reward profiles and capital requirements
claim: Day trading requires more capital, generates commissions per trade, has overnight gap risk. Swing trading requires less capital, lower turnover, but faces multi-day drawdowns and overnight gaps.

source.section: Pros and cons of swing and day trading

mechanism: Timeframe determines exposure to different risk factors: intraday volatility, overnight news, liquidity conditions.
assumptions: Capital requirements are uniform; no portfolio margin or reduced requirements
failure_modes: Execution costs have changed; high-frequency traders have different capital requirements
validation: Backtest: measure execution costs, capital utilization, and drawdown by trading style; compare vs risk-free rate.
